reason: Recommend MedCPT for this expanded bounded evaluation: it had higher P@5, Recall@5, and nDCG than BioClinicalBERT, while hybrid and cross-encoder profiles added latency without a consistent quality improvement. BioClinicalBERT remains the dense fallback and PostgreSQL FTS remains available as the low-dependency lexical baseline.
quality_improvement: MedCPT improved P@5 from 0.017 to 0.058 and Recall@5 from 0.083 to 0.292 versus BioClinicalBERT on this 48-case evaluation; the earlier 25-patient smoke evaluation favored BioClinicalBERT.
latency_cost: Cross-encoder reranking increased median latency to approximately 119-248 ms versus approximately 16-58 ms for first-stage profiles.
limitations: 48 cases from one bounded synthetic Synthea sample
PubMed-oriented model training may not match synthetic FHIR phrasing
